# Parameters

<!-- Generated by `npm run params` from packages/engine/src/tuning.ts and profiles.ts. Edit those, not this file. -->

Every fine-tuning knob of the engine, with its default, the range a family can choose from, and why the default is what it is. Values outside the range are clamped.

## Per learner: set by the family

| Setting | Children 10–11 | Children 12–13 | Parents |
|---|---|---|---|
| Session length, minutes: default (range) | 10 (5–15) | 12 (5–15) | 15 (5–30) |
| Sessions per day: default (range) | 2 (1–5) | 2 (1–5) | 2 (1–5) |
| Minimum break between sessions, minutes | 90 | 90 | 60 |
| New units per day, at most | 10 | 14 | 20 |
| Reminders per day, at most | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| Answer modes | choices, voice, short-text | choices, voice, short-text, maths, free-text | choices, voice, short-text, maths, free-text |
| Who sees progress | parents and child, same view | parents and child, same view | only the learner |

## Engine tuning: same for the whole family unless changed

### Target recall

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Target recall, everyday units <br>`retention.base` | 0.9 | 0.75–0.97 | Above ~0.9 the review load grows steeply for little gain (FSRS workload curves). |
| Target recall, foundational units <br>`retention.foundational` | 0.92 | 0.75–0.97 | Other units build on these, so forgetting them costs more. |
| Target recall, nice-to-know units <br>`retention.niceToKnow` | 0.85 | 0.7–0.95 | Cheaper upkeep for material that matters less. |
| Test window (days) <br>`retention.testWindowDays` | 7 | 1–21 | A week of higher targets before a test, not more: earlier cramming fades. |
| Target recall before a test <br>`retention.test` | 0.95 | 0.85–0.98 | Aim high only when it is about to be checked. |
| Target recall after a one-off test <br>`retention.maintenance` | 0.8 | 0.6–0.9 | Keeps old chapters alive at little cost. |

### Workload

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overload threshold (needed / budget) <br>`workload.overloadThreshold` | 1.1 | 1–2 | Relax targets when the work needed keeps exceeding the time agreed. |
| Target drop per unit of overload <br>`workload.dropPerOverload` | 0.05 | 0–0.2 | Gentle: a 50% overload lowers targets by 0.025. |
| Largest target drop <br>`workload.maxDrop` | 0.06 | 0–0.15 | Never below the maintenance level. |

### Question ladder

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recall questions from (stability, days) <br>`ladder.recallFromDays` | 3 | 1–14 | Pick among choices while a memory is fragile, then produce it. |
| Apply questions from (stability, days) <br>`ladder.applyFromDays` | 10 | 3–30 | Use on new material once recall is reliable (desirable difficulty). |
| Explain questions from (stability, days) <br>`ladder.explainFromDays` | 30 | 7–90 | Explaining why is the deepest check, kept for stable knowledge. |

### Session planner

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Priority weight, nice to know <br>`planner.weightNiceToKnow` | 0.7 | 0.1–2 | Relative priority when time is short. |
| Priority weight, expected <br>`planner.weightExpected` | 1 | 0.1–2 | Reference weight. |
| Priority weight, foundational <br>`planner.weightFoundational` | 1.4 | 0.1–3 | Foundations first when time is short. |
| Priority boost the day before a test <br>`planner.testBoost` | 1 | 0–3 | 1 doubles the priority on the eve of the test, fading over the test window. |
| Priority floor <br>`planner.riskFloor` | 0.05 | 0–0.2 | Units right at their target still get some priority. |
| Prerequisite counts as known from recall <br>`planner.prerequisiteRecall` | 0.8 | 0.5–0.95 | New units wait until what they build on is known. |
| Pause new material below accuracy <br>`planner.pauseNewBelow` | 0.7 | 0.4–0.9 | Struggling means consolidate first, not add more. |
| Halve new material below accuracy <br>`planner.halveNewBelow` | 0.8 | 0.5–0.95 | Most answers should succeed: learning is fastest around 85% success. |
| Time cost of a new unit (× a question) <br>`planner.newUnitCost` | 2 | 1–4 | Studying the card, then answering it. |

### Inside a session

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Easier unit after this many misses in a row <br>`session.easeOffAfterMisses` | 3 | 2–6 | Rebuild confidence before continuing. |
| End the session after this many misses in a row <br>`session.stopAfterMisses` | 5 | 3–10 | Past this point, re-teaching beats more questions. |

### Missions

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Share of a mission session on the mission <br>`mission.focusShare` | 1 | 0.5–1 | 1 = full focus; lower keeps a few at-risk reviews from other subjects alive. |
| Mission unit is secure from (stability, days) <br>`mission.secureStabilityDays` | 7 | 3–30 | Needs correct answers on separate days (successive relearning), not one good session. |
| Repair prerequisites below recall <br>`mission.repairBelowRecall` | 0.8 | 0.5–0.95 | Fix the foundations before building on them. |

### Reminders

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pause reminders from this self-start share <br>`reminders.selfStartShare` | 0.8 | 0.5–1 | The habit has formed; the reminder has done its job. |
| Self-start measured over (days) <br>`reminders.lookbackDays` | 14 | 7–28 | Two weeks smooths out holidays and busy days. |
| Minimum active days before pausing <br>`reminders.minActiveDays` | 7 | 3–14 | Do not conclude from too few days. |
| Every other day after this many ignored <br>`reminders.backoffAfterIgnored` | 3 | 2–10 | Back off, never escalate. |
| Stop reminding after this many ignored <br>`reminders.stopAfterIgnored` | 6 | 3–15 | Then parents see it in the weekly summary instead. |
| Reminder followed if a session starts within (min) <br>`reminders.followWindowMinutes` | 30 | 10–120 | Used to learn which time slot works for each child. |

### Memory model

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Longest gap between reviews (days) <br>`memory.maximumIntervalDays` | 365 | 30–3650 | A yearly check even on very stable memories. |
| Reviews needed before personal fitting <br>`memory.minReviewsToFit` | 400 | 100–2000 | Below this, defaults predict better than a fit. |
| Refit personal weights every (days) <br>`memory.refitEveryDays` | 7 | 1–30 | Weekly is enough; memory habits change slowly. |

### Learning by heart

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blank key words from (stability, days) <br>`byHeart.keyWordsFromDays` | 2 | 0.5–7 | First letters while the text is fresh, then only the small words stay. |
| Recite with nothing shown from (stability, days) <br>`byHeart.reciteFromDays` | 5 | 1–21 | Fading cues: the support disappears as memory takes over. |
| Recitation correct from (share of words in order) <br>`byHeart.passRatio` | 0.95 | 0.8–1 | Word for word means nearly every word, in order. |
| Recitation near miss from <br>`byHeart.nearMissRatio` | 0.85 | 0.6–0.98 | Close enough to come back soon, not from scratch. |

### Concentration profile

| Parameter | Default | Range | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Age default worth (sessions) <br>`concentration.priorWeight` | 5 | 1–30 | A few odd days must not swing the profile. |
| Focus ends at an accuracy drop of <br>`concentration.attentionDropPoints` | 0.15 | 0.05–0.4 | 15 points below the session start is a clear dip. |
| Focus ends at an answer-time rise of <br>`concentration.latencyRise` | 0.4 | 0.1–1 | Slowing down by 40% is the other sign of fatigue. |
| Chunk size holds from first-study success of <br>`concentration.chunkSuccessTarget` | 0.7 | 0.5–0.95 | Bigger chunks while 70% stick on first study; smaller below. |
| Group mixed reviews by subject above switch cost <br>`concentration.groupAboveSwitchCost` | 0.15 | 0–0.5 | Interleaving helps most learners; not one who loses 15 points per switch. |
